name: Sunday Times cryptic crossword, Penguin book 2 No 59

clue.text: Discharges outspoken teams
Distinctive character. of a uranium plant
Final expedient one has to endure beside the seaside, perhaps
Prepare for publication in reverse of the trend
Sailor has to find an answer to acquit
Sportsmen take unusual risks without direction
This new design for my robe is the start of something
Parliamentarians in the dark, yet still active?
Annoying weed?
Regret the past when imprisoned again?
One real upset for the queen
Make a mistake during the jaunt
Running from one thing to another, is placed by scoundrels in a disreputable haunt
Has personal saint?
The fruit of advanced age?
Register a wavelike flow
A lake likewise likewise!
Cleans up and cancels inferior teams
Abashed to get a deduction — can need changing
‘Thou shalt not kill; but need’st not — Officiously to keep alive’ (Clough: The Latest Decalogue)
Ugh! That unending body may be the cause of a sinful notion
Where sleepers have to put up with stresses?
County that Scott’s writing put heart into?
Definitely (or indefinitely!) this word can take up a few columns
More meaningless English politician has a row
State without women in a dull condition!
Girl partially rivalling Pamela in excellence
Noisy person in the rear or otherwise
Penalty for striking?
Carry heavy animal
